page: UpCloud DEV-2xCPU-8GB is a developer-class virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 2 vCPUs allocated on a shared basis, 2 physical cores, and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is bundled with 80 GB of SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. Single-core execution is highly efficient, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top tier. However, multi-core and memory write operations show significant limitations. Multi-core stress-ng performance and static web serving throughput sit in the average tier, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core scores, and Passmark CPU scores fall into the weak category. Memory write bandwidth for large blocks is poor, as is the Passmark memory score and software compilation performance.

Positioned within the Developer family, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for non-production environments, testing, and lightweight applications. The shared CPU allocation and weak multi-core scaling make it less suitable for heavy parallel processing, database operations, or intensive software compilation. Instead, the server is best utilized for single-threaded tasks, basic web serving, light LLM inference with small models, and general-purpose development or staging workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance.
